text.autoconfig.abadoned_greatwork.title: Abadoned Greatwork
text.autoconfig.abadoned_greatwork.optio: When enabled, the Eye of Locating sends its direction and the found target position to the summoner once it has found and turned toward the target.
text.abadoned_greatwork.eye.tooltip: Right-click to throw it; it hunts for its target and returns as an item if it fails
text.abadoned_greatwork.crystal.length_e: Error: spell total length exceeds crystal limit (%s)!
text.abadoned_greatwork.crystal.no_input: Error: crystal has no input data!
text.abadoned_greatwork.crystal.no_outpu: Error: crystal has no output data!
text.abadoned_greatwork.crystal.wrong: Verification failed: stack result does not match expected output!
text.abadoned_greatwork.crystal.success_: Phew, looks like I've gotten quite good at this.
text.abadoned_greatwork.riddles.add: Start with the simple, master addition and subtraction.
text.abadoned_greatwork.riddles.add.long: Submit a list of patterns that performs addition.
text.abadoned_greatwork.riddles.bigger: Given two numbers, find the larger.
text.abadoned_greatwork.riddles.bigger.l: Submit a list of patterns that takes two numbers, compares them, and returns the larger one.
text.abadoned_greatwork.riddles.block: Knowing the center, discern all eight directions.
text.abadoned_greatwork.riddles.block.lo: Submit a list of patterns that takes a position vector and returns a list of the eight adjacent vectors on the same horizontal plane (parallel to XZ) plus the vector itself, all floored, sorted with Themistian Purification.
text.abadoned_greatwork.riddles.block_cu: Through all six directions, seek the twenty-seven points of the cube.
Submit a list of patterns that takes a position vector and returns all 27 coordinates in a cube of edge length 3 centered on it, all floored, sorted with Themistian Purification.
text.abadoned_greatwork.riddles.cross: As the right-hand rule dictates, the logic of the cross product.
text.abadoned_greatwork.riddles.cross.lo: Submit a pattern or list of patterns that performs cross product, a fundamental vector operation.
text.abadoned_greatwork.riddles.absolute: Know this and that, know the distance between.
Submit a list of patterns that takes two position vectors and returns the distance between them.
text.abadoned_greatwork.riddles.mix: Three edges complete, three dimensions whole.
text.abadoned_greatwork.riddles.mix.long: Submit a list of patterns that takes three vectors and returns their scalar triple product — the volume of the parallelepiped they span, as a positive value.
hexcasting.page.abandoned_greatwork.1: The ancients left behind, and those who come after follow. I am neither the first Hex Caster, nor will I be the last.$(br2)Across the world, ruins left by ancient Hex Casters are scattered about. Though abandoned and cast into the mundane world, these structures still reflect the glory and brilliance they once held as Greatworks.
hexcasting.page.abandoned_greatwork.2: It seems the Hex Casters of old also created a special material to test the skill of their apprentices. Those who passed the trial would receive a reward.$(br2)Unfortunately, my records on this are not yet detailed enough. I should conduct more in-depth research when the opportunity arises.
advancements.abadoned_greatwork.root.des: Explore ruins left by ancient hexcasters
advancements.abadoned_greatwork.attempt_: Try to solve a Truth Crystal puzzle
advancements.abadoned_greatwork.solve_pu: Successfully pass a Truth Crystal verification
advancements.abadoned_greatwork.visit_ru: Discover a Ruined Circle structure in the Overworld
Discover a Ruined Circle structure in the Nether
Discover a Ruined Circle structure in the Deep Dark
abadoned_greatwork.category.text.desc: The glory of ages past now lies in ruin — today's works shall share this fate.
hexcasting.page.truth_crystal.1: One of the relics left by ancient hexcasters is the $(l)Truth Crystal$(). These mysterious crystals appear to have been used as testing tools — designed to evaluate the skill of an apprentice by challenging them to produce specific spell patterns.$(br2)A Truth Crystal contains a riddle with a description, and a length limit for submitted patterns. The aspiring hexcaster must solve the riddle to discover the correct pattern list.
hexcasting.page.truth_crystal.3: To attempt a riddle, place the Truth Crystal into a $(l)Truth Crystal Base$(), then right-click the base while holding an Iota-containing item. The crystal will evaluate your spell and judge the result.$(br2)If successful, the crystal will be consumed and a reward will be granted from a loot table specific to that crystal.
hexcasting.page.truth_crystal.crafting: Knowledge lies buried in history, wisdom cast aside in the dust of ages.
hexcasting.page.truth_crystal_patterns.c: Crystal Gazing requires a $(l)Truth Crystal$() held in the offhand. It consumes no media and displays the detailed information stored within the crystal in chat. Takes no input and produces no output.
hexcasting.page.truth_crystal_patterns.s: Truth Crystals demand strict output ordering. This pattern takes a list, rearranges its elements according to an intrinsic ordering, and returns the sorted list.
hexcasting.page.locator_patterns.eye_of_: An Eye of Locating, thrown like an Eye of Ender, flies a short distance, then hovers and searches the surroundings. If it senses the target biome or structure nearby, it turns to face it. After a while it shatters — or, more often, drops back as an item still bearing its target, ready to be thrown again.
hexcasting.page.locator_patterns.locate: Takes a $(l)Biome Token$() and summons an Eye of Locating that flies toward the target biome or structure. Costs a charged amethyst.
hexcasting.page.locator_patterns.random_: With equal odds it picks a random biome or a random structure, returning it wrapped as a $(l)Biome Token$(). Paired with Locate, it begins a journey of serendipity.
hexcasting.page.locator_patterns.current: Returns a $(l)Biome Token$() of the biome the caster currently stands in. Sometimes mishaps happen.
hexcasting.page.hex_eyes.tracking_item: An $(l)Eye of Tracking$() chases the target creature relentlessly. Once it reaches a spot above it, it hovers for a while and then shatters.
hexcasting.page.hex_eyes.waypoint_item: An $(l)Eye of Waypoint$() flies to a chosen place and hovers there, marking the spot. Once it arrives it lingers a while, then breaks with a burst of light.
hexcasting.page.hex_eyes.tracking_eye: Takes a $(l)vector$() (summon position) and an $(l)entity$() (target); summons an $(l)Eye of Tracking$() at that position, which takes that entity as its target. Costs a charged amethyst.
hexcasting.page.hex_eyes.waypoint_eye: Takes two $(l)vectors$() (summon position and destination); summons an $(l)Eye of Waypoint$() at that position, which flies to the destination coordinates. Costs amethyst dust.
hexcasting.mishap.abadoned_greatwork.con: Media wave from another impetus (%s) collided at Confluence Directrix (%s)
hexdoc.abadoned_greatwork.title: Abadoned Greatwork
text.abadoned_greatwork.crystal.wrong_ro: Verification failed (Round %s): stack result does not match expected output!
text.abadoned_greatwork.riddles.midpoint: Hold the center, halve the distance to find the heart.
Submit a list of patterns that takes two position vectors and returns the midpoint coordinate between them.
text.abadoned_greatwork.riddles.manhatta: Crisscross steps, measuring distance along gridlines.
Submit a list of patterns that takes two vectors and returns the Manhattan distance between them (sum of absolute differences of components).
text.abadoned_greatwork.riddles.list_rev: Reverse head and tail, tracing the stream upstream.
Submit a list of patterns that takes a list of two elements, swaps them, and returns the reversed list.
text.abadoned_greatwork.riddles.projecti: Cast a shadow with light, finding the projection along the path.
Submit a list of patterns that takes vector a and unit direction vector b, returning the projection vector of a onto b ((a·b) * b).
text.abadoned_greatwork.riddles.reflecti: A still mirror on water, refracting light to reveal the angle.
Submit a list of patterns that takes incident vector v and unit normal vector n, returning the reflected vector v - 2*(v·n)*n.
text.abadoned_greatwork.riddles.list_sum: Gather grains into a mound, sum all parts into the whole.
Submit a list of patterns that takes a list of three numbers and returns their sum.
text.abadoned_greatwork.riddles.collinea: Three stars in a line, judging straightness across space.
Submit a list of patterns that takes three position vectors a, b, c and returns a boolean indicating whether they are collinear.
text.abadoned_greatwork.riddles.clamp: Neither too much nor too little, bound within limits.
text.abadoned_greatwork.riddles.clamp.lo: Submit a list of patterns that takes number x, lower bound low, and upper bound high, returning x clamped to [low, high].
text.abadoned_greatwork.riddles.axial_ne: Within the six directions, adjacent guards of the axes.
Submit a list of patterns that takes a position vector and returns its 6 direct axial adjacent neighbors (up, down, east, west, north, south), floored, sorted with Themistian Purification.
text.abadoned_greatwork.riddles.filter_p: Discard the chaff, keeping only what is pure and positive.
Submit a list of patterns that takes a list of three numbers and filters out non-positive values, returning only positive numbers.
text.abadoned_greatwork.riddles.apply_tw: A second iteration, recurring to reach perfection.
Submit a list of patterns that takes number x at stack base and pattern list f at stack top, applying f twice to x and returning the result.
hexcasting.page.confluence_directrix.1: An ordinary $(l:greatwork/directrix)$(item)Directrix/$ chooses only one path at a time. Yet after studying fragments from ancient ruins, I realized a $(media)media/$ wave can branch along multiple routes simultaneously — provided a mind both sharp enough and divided enough guides it.$(br2)An ordinary villager's mind falters when split too far; only an illager practiced in commanding multiple manifestations at once can endure such division.
hexcasting.page.confluence_directrix.emp: Combining an $(l:greatwork/directrix)$(item)Empty Directrix/$ with emeralds and charged amethyst yields an $(item)Empty Confluence Directrix/$.$(br2)Sneak and $(k:use) any of its six faces to cycle that face through $(thing)Unconnected/$, $(thing)Input/$, and $(thing)Output/$.
hexcasting.page.confluence_directrix.2: When a $(media)media/$ wave enters an $(item)Empty Confluence Directrix/$, it forks copies of the stack and $(thing)Ravenmind/$ across every connected $(thing)Output/$ face in true parallel; the $(l:greatwork/impetus)$(item)Impetus/$ finishes only after every active branch concludes.$(br2)With two or more $(thing)Input/$ faces, earlier waves wait at the node until all inputs arrive: their stacks concatenate bottom-to-top in arrival order, while the final arrival's $(thing)Ravenmind/$ prevails. However, should $(media)media/$ waves from different $(l:greatwork/impetus)$(item)Impetuses/$ collide at the same Confluence Directrix, the conflicting sources immediately trigger a $(l:casting/mishaps)$(thing)Mishap/$!
hexcasting.page.confluence_directrix.evo: Casting $(l:patterns/great_spells/brainsweep)$(action)Flay Mind/$ on an $(thing)Evoker/$ into a placed $(item)Empty Confluence Directrix/$ awakens its inner core into an $(item)Evoker's Confluence Directrix/$, preserving existing port settings.
hexcasting.page.confluence_directrix.3: An $(item)Evoker's Confluence Directrix/$ can hold a single stored $(thing)pattern/$ (without one, it behaves like an $(item)Empty Confluence Directrix/$).$(br2)$(l)On Merge/$ (2+ inputs): the raw stack is replaced by one list per arrival in arrival order, each formatted as $(thing)[stack_list, ravenmind_or_null, enter_dir_vec]/$, and the stored pattern executes once.$(br2)$(l)On Split/$: for each valid $(thing)Output/$ face, its outgoing $(thing)unit direction vector/$ is pushed onto an isolated copy before executing the stored pattern once per branch; a mishap stops only that branch.
hexcasting.page.wireless_media_wave.1: Why... Time after time I wiped out every hateful raider, leaving not a single living scout to carry word home—and yet those sickening horns still sound right on cue along the village rim?$(br2)Hexcasting may be lost to them, yet these crude minds still retain an instinctive trick with media: bouncing waves around a closed loop to broadcast across empty air toward another isolated circle.
hexcasting.page.wireless_media_wave.2: I freed the spirits sealed within quenched crystal and flayed illager minds into relay and impetus stone—half-hoping to turn closed circuits completely open at last.$(br2)When the first assembly snapped together, a cold dread struck me: their consciousness is anything but natural. Stripped into circle components, it fits with $(l)zero friction/$—almost as if they were engineered for this.
hexcasting.page.wireless_media_wave.tran: $(l:patterns/great_spells/brainsweep)$(action)Flaying the Mind/$ of a $(thing)Raid Captain/$ into a placed $(item)Quenched Allay Block/$ awakens its wireless core, creating an $(item)Illager Wave Transmitter/$.

Places on all six faces (sneak to flip) with four banner facings. Wired in series on a circle, passing waves radiate the stack and $(thing)Ravenmind/$ while continuing along the sender's ring.$(br)It radiates as a dipole—weakest along the mast axis, strongest broadside—out to $(thing)8 + 6 × slates/$ blocks (cap $(thing)256/$). Empty-hand $(k:use) cycles channels $(thing)0..15/$, or write any custom $(thing)Iota/$ onto it.
hexcasting.page.wireless_media_wave.repe: Forging a $(item)Goat Horn/$ with $(item)Slates/$, $(item)Charged Amethyst/$, and $(item)Quenched Allay Shards/$ yields a $(item)Media Wave Repeater/$ for long-range links.

Can sit upright or upside-down across four horizontal facings.$(br)Standing alone, it catches matching waves and relays them $(thing)2/$ ticks later with $(thing)1.25×/$ forward range ahead of the horn ($(thing)+4/$ equivalent slates, min $(thing)5/$, up to $(thing)8/$ loop-free hops).$(br)Wired into slates directly, it also serves as a forward-boosted directional transmitter.
hexcasting.page.wireless_media_wave.rece: $(l:patterns/great_spells/brainsweep)$(action)Flaying the Mind/$ of any $(thing)Illager/$ (Pillager, Vindicator, Evoker, or Illusioner) into an $(l:greatwork/impetus)$(item)Empty Impetus/$ produces a $(item)Pillager Impetus/$.

A $(item)Pillager Impetus/$ acts as a wireless Impetus firing out its embossed face (1-second cooldown). Upon catching a matching wave, it starts execution with the sender's stack and $(thing)Ravenmind/$ loaded into its first frame.$(br2)One constraint remains: while media bridges empty air between sender and receiver without slates, the receiving circle $(l)must still close back onto itself/$.
hexcasting.page.media_pool.1: Even the grandest spell circles often choke on an $(l:greatwork/impetus)$(item)Impetus/$'s limited media reserve before their work concludes.$(br2)By shaping quenched crystal and slate around a $(item)Phial of Media/$, I built an open reservoir capable of exchanging media cleanly with waves passing through a circle.
hexcasting.page.media_pool.recipe: Ring a $(item)Phial of Media/$ with $(item)Quenched Allay Shards/$ and $(item)Slates/$ to craft a $(item)Media Pool/$.
hexcasting.page.media_pool.2: Must be placed flat upright; holds up to $(thing)7680/$ Amethyst Dust (or $(thing)unlimited/$ if fueled with a $(item)Creative Unlocker/$). Right-click with Amethyst Dust, Shards, Charged Amethyst, or media holders to refill. Its liquid surface rises and falls with reserve, comparators read $(thing)0–15/$, and a $(item)Scrying Lens/$ shows exact stored Dust.
hexcasting.page.media_pool.3: When a spell wave passes through a $(item)Media Pool/$, it pops a finite $(thing)number n/$ from the stack top:$(br)$(li)$(thing)n > 0/$: moves $(media)n/$ Dust from the pool into the circle's Impetus ($(l:casting/mishaps)$(thing)Mishap/$ if pool lacks media);$(br)$(li)$(thing)n < 0/$: draws $(media)|n|/$ Dust from the Impetus into the pool ($(l:casting/mishaps)$(thing)Mishap/$ if Impetus lacks media);$(br)$(li)$(thing)n = 0/$: pops zero and passes through; an empty stack or non-number triggers a Mishap.
hexcasting.mishap.abadoned_greatwork.amb: Channel %s only has %s bound Waymark Pylons; at least 3 are needed to close a valid ambit
Reshaped ambit exceeds circle budget: needs %s blocks³ (%s × %s), circle cap is %s blocks³
Waymark Pylon at (%s) on Channel %s has no chain order assigned; Sneak+Use to set it
Channel %s has duplicate chain order #%s at (%s) and (%s)
hexcasting.page.vindicator_ambit.1: Evokers split their focus across minions, and Pillagers hail distant raids; yet $(thing)Vindicators/$ are the most obsessive $(l)wardens of boundaries/$ among illagers—guarding a single woodland corridor with axe raised to cleave life from death.$(br2)Flaying that territorial obsession into a directrix lets us carve a circle's rigid rectangular bounds into custom contours without conjuring a single block of extra volume.
hexcasting.page.vindicator_ambit.switch_: $(l:patterns/great_spells/brainsweep)$(action)Flaying the Mind/$ of a $(thing)Vindicator/$ into a placed $(l:greatwork/directrix)$(item)Empty Directrix/$ produces a $(item)Vindicator's Ambit Directrix/$.
hexcasting.page.vindicator_ambit.pylon_r: Combine $(item)Amethyst Shards/$, $(item)Slate/$, $(item)Iron Ingots/$, and $(item)Deepslate/$ to forge four slender $(item)Waymark Pylons/$.
hexcasting.page.vindicator_ambit.2: $(item)Vindicator's Ambit Directrix/$ places upright like a thick slate. Empty-hand $(k:use) cycles channels $(thing)0..15/$, or write any custom $(thing)Iota/$ for private tuning; using $(item)Waymark Pylons/$ on it imprints its channel onto the stack.$(br)Placed pylons start unassigned: empty-hand $(k:use) switches channels while sneaking empty-hand $(k:use) manually assigns chain rank ($(thing)#1, #2, #3.../$). When active in a circle, both pylon orbs and the closed boundary line glow with the caster's pigment or stack-top color until another ambit is applied or the cast ends.
hexcasting.page.vindicator_ambit.3: When a media wave traverses the directrix, it connects matching pylons in ascending manual rank into an even-odd polygon (including perimeter blocks and concave C-shapes) extruded from lowest to highest pylon, $(l)replacing/$ the branch's default box.$(br)An empty channel ($(thing)0/$ pylons) restores default bounds; $(thing)1–2/$ pylons, unassigned or duplicate ranks, or a volume $(thing)S × H/$ exceeding the original circle box triggers a $(l:casting/mishaps)$(thing)Mishap/$.

hexponder.scene.stack_and_grid.title: The Stack & Hex Grid
hexponder.scene.stack_and_grid.subtitle: How stack values pass between drawn patterns
hexponder.scene.stack_and_grid.k0.title: Casting Stack
hexponder.scene.stack_and_grid.k0.body: Casting passes iotas along a bottom-to-top stack: reflections add iotas while purifications consume top entries and return results.
hexponder.scene.stack_and_grid.k1.title: Hex Grid
hexponder.scene.stack_and_grid.k1.body: Patterns trace continuous lines across grid dots without reusing an edge; only turn angles matter, not start spot or heading.
hexponder.scene.stack_and_grid.s0.tip: Mind's Reflection pushes the caster onto the stack
hexponder.scene.stack_and_grid.s1.tip: Compass' Purification replaces the entity with its eye vector
hexponder.scene.stack_and_grid.s2.tip: Push the caster once more for the next step
hexponder.scene.stack_and_grid.s4.tip: Reveal prints the top vector while keeping it on the stack
hexponder.scene.iotas_overview.title: Iota Overview
hexponder.scene.iotas_overview.subtitle: Numbers, vectors, booleans, lists, Null, and Garbage
hexponder.scene.iotas_overview.k0.title: Basic Iotas
hexponder.scene.iotas_overview.k0.body: The stack holds numbers, vectors, entities, and booleans to track counts, coordinates, beings, and truth values.
hexponder.scene.iotas_overview.k1.title: Lists & Null
hexponder.scene.iotas_overview.k1.body: Lists bundle multiple iotas including patterns; Null marks the absence of a valid target.
hexponder.scene.iotas_overview.s0.title: Number: 3.14
hexponder.scene.iotas_overview.s0.tip: Numbers represent distances, weights, and indices
hexponder.scene.iotas_overview.s1.title: Vector: {1, 2, 3}
hexponder.scene.iotas_overview.s1.tip: Positions and sight directions live in 3D vectors
hexponder.scene.iotas_overview.s2.title: Boolean
hexponder.scene.iotas_overview.s3.title: List
hexponder.scene.iotas_overview.s3.tip: Lists hold both values and stored pattern sequences
hexponder.scene.iotas_overview.s4.title: Null
hexponder.scene.iotas_overview.s4.tip: Missed raycasts return Null; guard for Null before use
hexponder.scene.actions_and_spells.title: Stack Order & Math
hexponder.scene.actions_and_spells.subti: Shaping stack order with Gemini and Jester's Gambit
hexponder.scene.actions_and_spells.k0.bo: Subtraction, division, and targeted spells distinguish the deeper first entry from the topmost second entry.
hexponder.scene.actions_and_spells.k1.bo: Gemini Decomposition, Jester's Gambit, and Prospector's Gambit rearrange values without re-casting queries.
hexponder.scene.actions_and_spells.s0.ti: Only a single 10 sits on the stack
hexponder.scene.actions_and_spells.s1.ti: Gemini Decomposition splits 10 into two copies
hexponder.scene.actions_and_spells.s3.ti: Jester's Gambit swaps 3 and 10 to compute 3 - 10
hexponder.scene.avoid_mishaps.title: Mishaps & Hygiene
hexponder.scene.avoid_mishaps.subtitle: How missing operands trigger mishaps and how to clear leftovers
hexponder.scene.avoid_mishaps.k0.title: Mishaps
hexponder.scene.avoid_mishaps.k0.body: Drawing an action with too shallow a stack or the wrong iota type triggers a mishap, stalling the cast or draining media.
hexponder.scene.avoid_mishaps.k1.title: Sweeping the Stack
hexponder.scene.avoid_mishaps.k1.body: Bookkeeper's Gambit drops chosen slots by teeth profile, while Thanatos' Reflection helps clear the top.
hexponder.scene.avoid_mishaps.s0.title: Number: 5
hexponder.scene.avoid_mishaps.s1.tip: Addition needs two numbers; having only one raises a mishap
hexponder.scene.avoid_mishaps.s2.tip: Bookkeeper's Gambit trims away unwanted top items
hexponder.scene.avoid_mishaps.s3.tip: Thanatos tidies leftovers before the next stroke
hexponder.scene.escape_and_parens.title: Consideration & Parens
hexponder.scene.escape_and_parens.subtit: Deferring evaluation to capture one pattern or build a list
hexponder.scene.escape_and_parens.k0.bod: Drawing Consideration prevents only the very next pattern from running, pushing it onto the stack instead.
hexponder.scene.escape_and_parens.k1.bod: Introspection opens a bracket layer to collect patterns until matching Retrospection closes them into one list.
hexponder.scene.escape_and_parens.s0.tip: Consideration primes Esc to catch the next stroke
hexponder.scene.escape_and_parens.s1.tip: Additive Distillation lands on the stack as a pattern instead of running
hexponder.scene.escape_and_parens.s3.tip: Introspection raises parens: drawn patterns collect inside
hexponder.scene.escape_and_parens.s6.tip: Retrospection closes the parens into a two-pattern list
hexponder.scene.logics.title: Branching Logic
hexponder.scene.logics.subtitle: Checking for Null, selecting with Augur, and running with Hermes
hexponder.scene.logics.k0.title: Augur's Exaltation
hexponder.scene.logics.k0.body: Takes [condition, ifTrue, ifFalse] from bottom to top: true keeps the first option, false keeps the second.
hexponder.scene.logics.k1.title: Wrap Before Selecting
hexponder.scene.logics.k1.body: Wrap both options in brackets first, pick the winner with Augur, then unfold only that winner via Hermes' Gambit.
hexponder.scene.logics.s4.tip: Returns the hit block vector, or Null when facing open sky
hexponder.scene.logics.s6.tip: Turns the hit result into a clear boolean with Null and Inequality
hexponder.scene.logics.s14.tip: The stack holds condition, true branch, and false branch
hexponder.scene.logics.s15.tip: Augur discards the unchosen branch, leaving the winner on top
hexponder.scene.logics.s16.tip: Hermes' Gambit runs only the chosen spell list
hexponder.scene.thoth_foreach.title: Thoth Iteration
hexponder.scene.thoth_foreach.subtitle: Running one spell sequence across each item of a list
hexponder.scene.thoth_foreach.k0.title: Thoth's Gambit
hexponder.scene.thoth_foreach.k0.body: Expects the spell list underneath and the data list on top, running the spell in turn for each element.
hexponder.scene.thoth_foreach.k1.title: Collecting Results & Charon
hexponder.scene.thoth_foreach.k1.body: Leftover stack results from every pass gather into one list; Charon's Gambit stops iteration early.
hexponder.scene.thoth_foreach.s1.tip: Single's Purification wraps +Y into a one-item list
hexponder.scene.thoth_foreach.s5.title: Offset Vector
hexponder.scene.thoth_foreach.s8.title: Helper Vector
hexponder.scene.thoth_foreach.s10.tip: This bracketed sequence runs for every entry in the data list
hexponder.scene.thoth_foreach.s11.tip: Jester places the data list on top to match Thoth
hexponder.scene.thoth_foreach.s12.tip: Thoth finishes all passes and gathers the results
hexponder.scene.meta_and_continuation.su: Holding Ravenmind with Huginn/Muninn and breaking out with Iris + Charon
hexponder.scene.meta_and_continuation.k0: Ravenmind holds a single iota beside the stack: Huginn sets it and Muninn reads a copy without touching deeper items.
hexponder.scene.meta_and_continuation.k1: When running a list via Iris' Gambit, casting Charon's Gambit immediately exits the remainder of that list.
hexponder.scene.meta_and_continuation.s1: Huginn's Gambit tucks 42 away into Ravenmind
hexponder.scene.meta_and_continuation.s6: Gemini after Charon will never be reached once triggered
hexponder.scene.meta_and_continuation.s7: Iris unwinds at Charon, leaving only Muninn's read 42
hexponder.scene.raycast_and_lights.title: Raycast & Light
hexponder.scene.raycast_and_lights.subti: Combining hit position and surface normal before conjuring light
hexponder.scene.raycast_and_lights.k0.bo: Archer yields the solid block looked at; Architect yields its outward normal. Adding them targets the open air beside it.
hexponder.scene.raycast_and_lights.k1.bo: Patterns shown here trace stack behavior without altering nearby blocks around you.
hexponder.scene.raycast_and_lights.s4.ti: Yields the hit block position, or Null toward open sky
hexponder.scene.raycast_and_lights.s9.ti: Yields the unit direction pointing back toward you
hexponder.scene.raycast_and_lights.s14.t: Conjure Light completes here while leaving your surroundings untouched
hexponder.scene.quine_daemon.title: Self-Holding & List Edits
hexponder.scene.quine_daemon.subtitle: Unfolding lists with Splat, peeking deep items, and patching via Surgeon
hexponder.scene.quine_daemon.k0.title: Splat & Flock
hexponder.scene.quine_daemon.k0.body: Splat unfolds every element onto the stack, while Flock's Gambit packs the top N items back into a list.
hexponder.scene.quine_daemon.k1.title: Self-Reproducing Patterns
hexponder.scene.quine_daemon.k1.body: Certain pattern lists rebuild their own sequence on the stack when run, aiding cyclic spells.
hexponder.scene.quine_daemon.s0.title: Preset Self-Holding List
hexponder.scene.quine_daemon.s0.tip: Contains 12 patterns arranged to reconstruct themselves
hexponder.scene.quine_daemon.s1.tip: Splat unfolds all 12 patterns onto the stack
hexponder.scene.quine_daemon.s2.tip: Prospector copies the second-from-top entry upward
hexponder.scene.quine_daemon.s3.title: Pack Count: 2
